text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- An opposition representative to the Central Election Commission (CEC) says Italian observers to Sunday's local polls did not consider them fair.
- The paper says the Italian report lists serious irregularities. It alleges the Democrat Party chairman of a polling station offered them narcotics and money to refrain from pointing them out.
- The Socialist Party has told U.S. diplomats it considers that the recent local polls were manipulated.
- A man held as the main suspect in the killing of the general director of prisons has been released.
- An Albanian entrepreneur has returned $3.3 million to creditors four years after his business collapsed.
- Vefa Holding, one of Albania's biggest concerns, plans to build a four-star hotel at the seaside and to launch a 150-bed cruiser.
- Albania finally has recovered gold looted by the Nazis during World War Two and since held by an Anglo-French-American commission.
- An explosive device was planted outside the office of a Greek fuel trader in the southern town of Gjirokaster. No one was hurt in the blast.
- Ilir Meta, the leader of the Socialists Youth, called for changes in the party leadership after their defeat in the recent local polls.
- The discovery of a golden statuette from the first century A.D. on a beach near Durres has raised hopes among scholars that there may be an ancient temple nearby.
- A representative of the U.S. State Department has complimented the Democratic Party on holding free and fair elections on October 20.
- Albania's defence minister Safet Zhulali is in the United States. He will meet U.S. Secretary of Defence William Perry.
- The daily says the opposition Socialist Party, the reformed communists, who suffered a big defeat in the latest local polls, have a present and a future.
